To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calorie restriction delays the onset of muscle loss in adult monkeys, and prevents age-associated cellular phenotypes in muscle.
calorie restriction delays and prevents age-associated loss of muscle mass and muscle fiber CSA in rhesus monkeys.
calorie restriction (CR), a dietary intervention that reduces the incidence of multiple age-associated diseases, also preserves skeletal muscle in aged nonhuman primates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular basis for the delayed onset and slowed progression of sarcopenia in CR monkeys.
understanding the cellular mechanisms of muscle aging and the impact of CR on muscle aging.
the mechanisms of aging, and the preservation of muscle mass in the face of age-related changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
calorie restriction is the only intervention that has been shown to prevent the loss of skeletal muscle mass in aged primates.
calorie restriction delays the onset of muscle loss in aging rhesus monkeys, preserves fiber number and muscle mass and prevents age-related muscle fiber phenotypes.
CR prevents the age-associated changes in muscle fiber composition and muscle mass loss in rhesus monkeys.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CR is a powerful tool for the prevention of age-related muscle loss and that muscle aging is a complex process that is impacted by the interplay between multiple cell types, including myocytes, adipocytes, and fibroblasts.
a 30-40% CR diet preserves muscle mass and fiber number in rhesus monkey skeletal muscle, and that the preservation of fiber number is a major contributor to the preservation of muscle mass.
the cellular and molecular adaptations that occur in skeletal muscle in adult and old monkeys are likely to contribute to the preservation of muscle mass in CR animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calorie restriction can preserve the quality of skeletal muscle in very old monkeys and may be a useful strategy for maintaining muscle mass in the elderly.
CR can prevent or delay many cellular phenotypes of muscle aging in adult rhesus monkeys and preserve skeletal muscle mass and fiber density into advanced age.
calorie restricted monkeys are protected from the loss of muscle mass, muscle fiber CSA, and muscle fiber density that is characteristic of aging in monkeys and humans.
